findings.issue: Particle annotations are swapped: in the JP, を marks 小説 (romances) and が marks 方 (o lado), but the literal gloss attaches (を) to 'escrever' and (が) to 'romances', teaching the wrong structural mapping in the field whose job is to mirror structure.
findings.current: Quanto a (isto), o lado de escrever (を) romances (が) é o forte.
findings.suggested: Quanto a (isto), o lado (が) de escrever romances (を) é o forte.

findings.issue: Same swapped particle annotations as lit_pt: を belongs to 小説 (novels) and が to 方 (the side/option), but the gloss attaches (を) to 'the writing' and (が) to 'novels', misrepresenting which constituent each particle marks.
findings.current: As for this, the writing (を) of novels (が) is the strong point.
findings.suggested: As for this, the side (が) of writing novels (を) is the strong point.

findings.issue: そちら means 'that side / your side' (near the listener), not 'this side' (= こちら). The lit_pt ('desse lado'), the token gloss and both explanations all correctly say 'that side'; lit_en teaches the wrong demonstrative mapping.
findings.current: As for the option on this side (の+ほう) (が), it is appropriate.
findings.suggested: As for the option on that side (near you) (の+ほう) (が), it is appropriate.

findings.issue: 発症 is the verbal-noun base of the compound verb 発症する, not an object — the clause's real object is 病気を, so 'objeto' puts two objects in one clause. The corpus's own convention labels this slot 'substantivo verbal' (cf. コピー in jec-4591, 放送 in jec-4753).
findings.suggested: substantivo verbal (base de 発症する)

findings.issue: Mixed-script typo: 'полido' is written with Cyrillic letters (пол + Latin ido) instead of 'polido'.
findings.current: Graças (a você) (で), de algum jeito, o hoje (を) receber (こと が) consegui (полido, passado).
findings.suggested: Graças (a você) (で), de algum jeito, o hoje (を) receber (こと が) consegui (polido, passado).

findings.issue: ディレクトリ (でぃれくとり) is romanized 'deirekutori'; でぃ is pronounced 'di', so it should be 'direkutori' — 'dei' misrepresents the pronunciation as で+い.
